extracted.intended_audience: politicians, statesmen, legislators, and informed public concerned with governance and public policy (late 18th-century Britain)
extracted.subtask_description: Normative criteria and standards for judging statesmen, legislative acts, and public policy—especially in the context of revolutions, confiscation of property, and institutional reform. Emphasises justice, prudence, preservation of institutions, and practical improvement over violent innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenacity of justice and tenderness of property in reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: In all mutations (if mutations must be) the circumstance which will serve most to blunt the edge of their mischief, and to promote what good may be in them, is, that they should find us with our minds tenacious of justice, and tender of property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When undertaking change, maintain commitment to justice and protection of property to reduce harm; prefer measures that preserve rights and legal stability rather than radical expropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice as the primary policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice is itself the great standing policy of civil society; and any eminent departure from it, under any circumstances, lies under the suspicion of being no policy at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposed state measures primarily by their conformity with justice; departures from justice should be treated with suspicion even when justified as 'policy'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of a statesman: preserve and improve
rubrics_metrics.description: A disposition to preserve, and an ability to improve, taken together, would be my standard of a statesman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good statesmanship combines conservatism (preserving valuable existing structures) with practical capacity to make improvements; neither pure destruction nor mere preservation is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer reformation and adaptation over total destruction
rubrics_metrics.description: There is something else than the mere alternative of absolute destruction, or unreformed existence. Spartam iiuactu es; hanc exorna. ... I cannot conceive how any man can have brought himself to that pitch of presumption, to consider his country as nothing but carte blanche.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek intermediate, corrective reforms that adapt and adorn existing institutions rather than annihilate them; avoid presumptuous overhaul treating the polity as blank slate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to arbitrary legislative degradation and confiscation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is unjust in legislature, by an arbitrary act, to offer a sudden violence to their minds and their feelings; forcibly to degrade them from their state and condition, and to stigmatize with shame and infamy that character and those customs which before had been made the measure of their happiness and honour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislation should not subject persons or groups to abrupt deprivation of property, status, or livelihood without just process; such acts verge on tyranny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confiscation during revolutions is dangerous and unpredictable
rubrics_metrics.description: Revolutions are favourable to confiscation; and it is impossible to know under what obnoxious names the next confiscations will be authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware that confiscatory measures set precedents and can be extended arbitrarily; evaluate long-term political consequences of sanctioning confiscation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare old possessors with proposed purchasers before transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: A sober legislator would carefully compare the possessor whom he was recommended to expel, with the stranger who was proposed to fill his place. Before the inconveniences are incurred... we ought to have some rational assurance that the purchasers of the confiscated property will be in a considerable degree more laborious, more virtuous, more sober...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy that transfers property must justify that new owners will use it more productively or virtuously; do not assume dispossessed are worse merely by status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of corporate/standing institutions for long-term projects
rubrics_metrics.description: The perennial existence of bodies corporate and their fortunes are things particularly suited to a man who has long views ... Wisdom cannot create materials; her pride is in the use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve permanent institutions and their endowments because they enable long-term projects (libraries, collections, scientific specimens, monuments) that individual, transient owners might not sustain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate bodies are more amenable to public direction than private citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: In a question of reformation, I always consider corporate bodies... to be much more susceptible of a public direction by the power of the state, in the use of their property, and in the regulation of modes and habits of life in their members, than private citizens ever can be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer using public authority to reform or direct corporate bodies' uses and comportment rather than dispossessing them; state direction can achieve public ends without confiscation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerate lesser social errors to avoid worse outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Superstition is the religion of feeble minds; and they must be tolerated... Prudence would be neuter; but... perhaps he would think the superstition which builds, to be more tolerable than that which demolishes...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In managing social passions and institutions, choose the lesser evil—tolerate benign or constructive errors (that 'build' or 'adorn') rather than destructive ones that harm society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public expenditure should return surplus to industry with minimal moral detriment
rubrics_metrics.description: The only concern of the state is, that the capital taken in rent from the land, should be returned again to the industry from whence it came; and that its expenditure should be with the least possible detriment to the morals of those who expend it, and to those of the people to whom it is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative concern is to ensure that landed surplus circulates back into productive industry and that its distribution does not corrupt morals or harm laborers; evaluate transfers with this circulation test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume new proprietors will spend more wisely or virtuously
rubrics_metrics.description: It does not appear to me, that the expenses of those whom you are going to expel, do, in fact, take a course so directly and so generally leading to vitiate and degrade... as the expenses of those favourites whom you are intruding into their houses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skepticism toward claims that new owners (post-confiscation purchasers) will necessarily be superior in virtue or benefit to the public; empirical comparison needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural and institutional spending can be as valuable as private expenditure
rubrics_metrics.description: Why should the expenditure of a great landed property... appear intolerable... when it takes its course through the accumulation of vast libraries, ... through paintings and statues ... through grand monuments of the dead ... through collections of the specimens of nature...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the public value of expenditures on culture, science, and monuments; institutional uses of surplus can benefit society and deserve protection from arbitrary confiscation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage public debt and taxation to avoid provoking powerful interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Nations are wading deeper and deeper into an ocean of boundless debt... If governments provide for these debts by heavy impositions, they perish by becoming odious to the people. If they do not provide for them, they will be undone by the efforts of the most dangerous of all parties; I mean an extensive, discontented monied interest, injured and not destroyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should balance debt repayment and taxation carefully: avoid crushing taxes that make government unpopular, but also avoid ignoring debts that could empower a discontented financial interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies should be grounded in experience, not untried speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: They commit the whole to the mercy of untried speculations; they abandon the dearest interest of the public to those loose theories to which none of them would choose to trust the slightest of his private concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public schemes must show empirical evidence or experience of benefit; avoid entrusting crucial public interests to speculative theories unsupported by practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy of power requires legal sanction and broad authority
rubrics_metrics.description: I can never consider this Assembly as any thing else than a voluntary association of men, who have availed themselves of circumstances to seize upon the power of the state. They have not the sanction and authority of the character under which they first met... The most considerable of their acts have not been done by great majorities; and in this sort of near divisions... strangers will consider reasons as well as resolutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating new governing bodies or revolutionary assemblies, assess whether their authority derives from established law or broad representative sanction; thin majorities weaken the moral force of acts and invite scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish eloquence from wisdom in judging leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: I am convinced that there are men of considerable parts among the popular leaders... Some of them display eloquence in their speeches and their writings. ... Eloquence may exist without a proportionable degree of wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not be swayed by rhetorical talent alone; evaluate leaders for practical wisdom, judgment, and tested ability to secure public good rather than mere oratorical skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid treating the country as a blank slate for speculative schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: A man full of warm speculative benevolence may wish his society otherwise constituted than he finds it; but a good patriot, and a true politician, always considers how he shall make the most of the existing materials of his country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reformers should adapt and work with existing social materials and institutions; radical re-foundations based on speculative benevolence risk unintended harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use public direction to correct corporate abuses rather than wholesale dispossession
rubrics_metrics.description: This ought not to hinder you from deriving from superstition itself any resources which may thence be furnished for the public advantage... It was your business to correct and mitigate every thing which was noxious in this passion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When institutions are flawed (e.g., monastic superstition), seek correction and mitigation through regulation and direction so as to derive public benefits, instead of immediately destroying the institutions and seizing assets.
